secrets.description: GitHub App ID for the bot account that owns app repos. Without this, app creation fails and no PRs can be opened. `default: ""` lets a self-app staging clone boot for UI work — github.init() degrades to disabled when this is empty (see services/github.js).

PEM private key for the GitHub App. Single-line with literal \n escape sequences; the loader un-escapes at startup. `staging_default: ""` pairs with GITHUB_APP_ID — both empty means github.init() takes the disabled branch and staging boots without GitHub features.

Classic PAT with `repo` scope for the bot user. Powers repo creation, branch pushes, PR creation, and the in-app feedback flow (Issues:write on USERNODE_PLATFORM_REPO). `staging_default: ""` lets staging boot — every consumer guards on `if (!pat)` and degrades.

Platform-wide fallback Claude key. Users can override with their own via BYOK; if neither is set, Mayor-driven flows are unavailable. Already optional, so no staging fallback needed — staging just inherits the unset state.

Bootstrap admin username. The first row in `users` is created with this name and is_admin=true on first boot. `default: "admin"` covers self-app staging (where the secrets UI is read-only and prod app_secrets is always empty); the staging DB clone already carries whatever admin row prod has, so this default only matters for a fresh-DB clone.

Bootstrap admin password. Hashed at first boot — rotating only takes effect on a fresh DB or via direct SQL update. `private` keeps a self-app-staging container from receiving the prod admin password (would let any PR reviewer log in as admin to prod). `staging_default` is a config.js boot-sentinel only — never used to authenticate. Self-app staging containers expose no usable password login: the cloned `users.password` column is replaced with `__staging_redacted__` by db-manager.scrubPrivateColumns, and staging admins authenticate via the parent-issued iframe JWT instead (see SELF-HOSTING.md "Self-staging — iframe-auth login flow" and middleware/auth.js).

Signing key for session JWTs and the iframe-issued tokens child apps verify (see app-conventions.md). Required at boot — config.js refuses to start without it. Rotating invalidates every active session. `private` ensures a self-app-staging container could not mint valid prod JWTs. NOTE: this entry is silently skipped by app-manifest.read() because JWT_SECRET is on the reserved-keys list (services/app-manifest.js); the platform injects the parent's value into staging containers explicitly via services/staging.js. Listed here for documentation only — no runtime effect.

Cookie-signing secret for express-session. Required at boot. Rotating invalidates every active session cookie. `private` for parallel reasons to JWT_SECRET — staging must never sign cookies that browsers honor for prod. `staging_default` is a deliberately distinguishable dummy so any cookie minted by staging is obviously not a prod cookie.

Postgres superuser password the platform connects with. Used by docker-compose.yml to seed the postgres container, by db-manager.js to spawn per-app databases, and baked into DATABASE_URL for the platform itself. Rotating means rolling the postgres container too. `private` blocks staging propagation of the prod DB superuser. `staging_default` is a placeholder — the staging container's DATABASE_URL is set explicitly to the staging clone's URL by services/staging.js, and db-manager.js falls back to 'localdev' when this is unfamiliar; spawning child apps from within a staging container is out of scope for UI-edit workflows.

Platform's on-chain wallet public key for the Usernode social-vibecoding linking flow (chain-poller + auth wallet-link in routes/auth.js). When unset, wallet-linking is gracefully disabled — the platform still works without it.

Private counterpart to USERNODE_APP_PUBKEY. Pre-staged in deploy.yml so any future platform-originated wallet-send flow can use it without a redeploy — currently no runtime consumer reads it. Always set together with USERNODE_APP_PUBKEY. `private` blocks staging propagation: this key signs real on-chain transactions with real funds.

platform_env.description: Log verbosity for the platform process: DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR. Raising it to DEBUG is the one tunable you actually want to change without a code change while chasing something in prod.
Ceiling on concurrent worker containers across the whole platform. The committed default targets ~50 concurrent users on a 20-core/62GB box; raise it only alongside WORKER_MEMORY headroom.
Ceiling on concurrent worker containers per user. Stops one person from consuming the whole global budget.
Docker memory limit for each worker container, in docker's own units (e.g. `1280m`). MAX_GLOBAL_SESSIONS × WORKER_MEMORY is the worst-case worker footprint.
Docker CPU limit for each worker container.
Maximum Postgres connections in the platform's pool. Must stay comfortably under the postgres container's own max_connections.
How long a worker container may sit idle before it is evicted to free a session slot.
Idle time before an active chat session is auto-paused. Paused sessions keep their state but release their worker.
How often the session sweeper runs the autopause/eviction pass.
When `true`, resuming a session under global pressure evicts the least-recently-used worker instead of refusing the resume.
Minimum age a session must reach before pressure-driven LRU eviction may take its worker.
How long an idle staging container survives before it is torn down. Staging is rebuilt on demand, so this trades disk and memory against the wait on the next preview.
Age at which an open proposal is flagged stale and its author notified.
Grace period after the stale notification before the proposal is archived.
How long archived proposals are retained before deletion.
How often the stale-proposal sweeper runs.
How long to wait for Caddy to obtain a certificate for a newly-published app subdomain before giving up on the warm-up.
Threshold above which a certificate probe is logged as slow.
Seconds docker waits after SIGTERM before killing a container. Raising it makes deploys slower but gives in-flight requests longer to drain.

Apex domain the platform and every app subdomain live under. Set from a GitHub repo variable by the deploy and listed here for documentation only — changing it needs the DNS and certificate change to land in the same breath, so it is deliberately not editable in the console.
Commit the running container was built from. Written by the deploy workflow from `github.sha`; documentation only.
Platform Postgres connection string, assembled by docker-compose from USERNODE_DB_PASSWORD. Documentation only — it is a reserved key and can never be written from here.
